ideia: A man buys a vintage mirror that reflects yesterday instead of today, until he sees himself waving back from behind the glass.
Every time a woman drinks coffee, her smartphone battery percentage drops by the exact same amount.
What if gravity reversed for exactly three seconds every Tuesday afternoon, but only inside grocery store freezer aisles?
An old clockmaker creates a grandfather clock that makes time run backward, only to realize it cannot be stopped once wound.
A houseplant refuses to grow unless its owner whispers daily compliments to it in a language nobody speaks.
A barista discovers that the foam art in her lattes predicts the trivial inconveniences her customers will face that day.
A detective finds a footprint on the ceiling of a locked room, only to realize the gravity inside the building is upside down.
What if shadows started lagging two seconds behind their people, mimicking actions before they actually happen?
A town librarian finds a book with no title that writes out every local resident's thoughts five minutes before they think them.
An ancient legend speaks of a mountain peak where echoes answer back with words nobody has spoken yet.
A late-night security guard notices the mannequins in a clothing store switch positions every time he blinks.
A man builds a robot to organize his sock drawer, but the machine unionizes with the laundry basket.
An amateur astronomer captures a star blinking in Morse code, spelling out his own childhood home address.
What if you could pay for items in a vending machine using your unused memories instead of cash?
A bakery uses flour from a mysterious mill where the bread baked reveals secret messages when sliced.
What if the moon was actually a giant lens focusing a stranger's flashlight onto our planet every night?
According to local legend, the town bell tolls thirteen times only when someone forgets their own name.
A smart refrigerator begins leaving passive-aggressive post-it notes on its own digital screen about the midnight snacking habits.
A tourist tries to use a universal translator app on a stray cat, only to receive stock market tips.
A woman receives daily letters from a secret admirer dated forty years in the future.
What if the color blue tasted like peppermint to everyone except left-handed people?
An antique compass points persistently toward the user's pocket instead of magnetic north.
The legend of the Whispering Woods says that if you lose an umbrella there, it returns as a tree branch.
A student wearing noise-canceling headphones realizes the silence in the room is getting louder.
A dog learns how to operate the television remote and refuses to watch anything except cooking shows.
A man finds a key in his pocket that unlocks doors he has not walked through yet.
What if every mirror on Earth was actually a window into a parallel universe where nobody has mirrors?
An art critic realizes a famous painting changes its background scenery whenever the gallery lights are turned off.
An old lighthouse keeps its light on even during sunny days to guide invisible ships away from the cliffs.
A person sets their alarm clock for tomorrow morning, but it starts ringing immediately from next week.
A smart home assistant starts locking the front door from the inside because it claims the porch is too loud.
A commuter accidentally boards a train that travels exclusively through yesterday's rush hour.
What if clouds were made of cotton candy, but only during thunderstorms?
A gardener finds a seed that sprouts flowers that glow in the dark and whisper secrets about the weather.
Legend has it that a forgotten fountain in the city park grants wishes, but only for parking spaces.
A phone charging cable refuses to work unless it is plugged in while facing away from the wall outlet.
An office worker discovers that his computer keyboard is typing out his inner thoughts instead of his emails.
What if elevators could move sideways through buildings if you pressed all the buttons in alphabetical order?
A painter realizes every portrait he paints ages instead of him, until the canvas starts smiling back independently.
A pigeon stands on a park bench and glares at a businessman because it believes the man owes it bread crumbs from last Tuesday.
